subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Placental Hormones: hCG and Human Placental Lactogen

steps.tx: The placenta functions as a temporary endocrine gland producing **placental hormones**. These maintain pregnancy, adapt maternal metabolism and prepare breasts for feeding. Their levels follow characteristic patterns used in screening and diagnosis. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: The placenta acts as a temporary endocrine gland adapting maternal metabolism for pregnancy.

steps.tx: The glycoprotein hormone detected by every pregnancy test is **human chorionic gonadotropin**. Produced by syncytiotrophoblast, it doubles about every forty eight hours in early viable pregnancy. Its beta subunit is what tests specifically measure. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Human chorionic gonadotropin from syncytiotrophoblast is what every pregnancy test measures.

steps.tx: Peak hCG occurs at about ten weeks then falls to a plateau, a pattern called the **hCG curve**. Abnormally slow rise suggests ectopic or failing pregnancy. Very high levels occur in molar pregnancy and multiple gestation. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: The hCG curve peaks at ten weeks, and slow rise suggests ectopic or failing pregnancy.

steps.tx: The placental hormone promoting maternal insulin resistance and lipolysis is **human placental lactogen**. It spares glucose for the fetus by making maternal tissues use fat instead. Its level reflects placental mass and function. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Human placental lactogen creates insulin resistance to spare glucose for the fetus.

steps.tx: Placental progesterone maintains uterine quietness throughout pregnancy, a state of **myometrial quiescence**. It also develops breast alveoli and suppresses maternal immune rejection of the fetus. Withdrawal near term in many animals triggers labour, though human mechanisms differ. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Progesterone maintains uterine quiescence, develops breasts and suppresses fetal rejection.

steps.tx: The main oestrogen of pregnancy made jointly by placenta and fetus is **oestriol**. Its production needs fetal adrenal precursors, so levels reflect fetal wellbeing. It rises steadily toward term and prepares the uterus for labour. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Oestriol is made jointly by fetus and placenta, so it reflects fetal wellbeing.

steps.tx: Excessive hCG explains several early pregnancy features through its weak thyroid action, termed **hCG thyroid stimulation**. It contributes to hyperemesis gravidarum severity. Twin and molar pregnancies exaggerate both hormone level and symptoms. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Excess hCG weakly stimulates the thyroid and worsens hyperemesis in twin and molar pregnancies.

steps.tx: Falling hCG after delivery or miscarriage is followed to zero in **trophoblast surveillance**. Persistent or rising levels after molar evacuation signal gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Contraception is advised during surveillance to avoid confusing a new pregnancy. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Trophoblast surveillance follows hCG to zero after molar evacuation to detect neoplasia.

steps.tx: Placental corticotropin releasing hormone rising toward term forms part of the **placental clock**. It is thought to time labour by stimulating fetal adrenal output. Abnormal timing links to preterm and post term labour patterns. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: The placental clock uses rising releasing hormone to help time labour near term.
